reading: The one-colour shape is reflected across its edge where the colour-2 marker cells touch it (the reflection covers the 2s); then all background becomes 3.
why: the axis is the line between the shape and its 2-marker cells; reflected shape lands exactly on the 2s; 0->3 everywhere else

reading: Every row or column whose interior (all cells except the two border cells) is entirely background is painted 3 on its background cells.

new_rows.name: clear_line
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
busy_row(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C), mx(M), X > 0, X < M.
busy_col(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), my(M), Y > 0, Y < M.
clear_line(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), !busy_row(Y).
clear_line(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), !busy_col(X).

why: a line is filled iff it has no non-background cell off the grid border; fill colour is always 3
invariants: background cells on lines that touch a wall cell inside

reading: A colour-3 path is drawn from the free end of the 2-cell green segment, going straight in the segment's direction, turning 90 degrees before obstacles / when aligned with the 2-cell red segment, until it touches the red segment.

slots.start: the 2-cell colour-3 segment (its direction gives the first heading)
slots.obstacles: colour-8 cells; path turns before hitting one
slots.turn: turn toward the goal; final leg enters the goal along its axis

why: the path is a chain of straight colour-3 runs that never crosses an 8 and ends adjacent to the 2-segment
invariants: all input cells keep their colour

reading: Each row is inverted against its own main colour: cells of the row's dominant non-background colour become 0, every other cell (0 or noise colour) becomes that dominant colour.

slots.row colour: the most frequent non-zero colour in that row
slots.rule: row colour -> 0; any other colour (including 0) -> row colour

why: in every output row only the row colour and 0 appear, exactly complementing the input's row-colour cells

reading: Each colour-9 block is cut by a zigzag band of 6s; the 6s become background and the two 9 pieces on either side of the band each move one cell away from it (perpendicular to the band).

slots.pieces: the 9 cells on each side of the band
slots.shift: each piece moves 1 cell away from the band, perpendicular to it (left/right for a vertical band, up/down for a horizontal band)

why: every output 9 cell is an input 9 cell shifted by one away from its object's 6 band; no 6 remains

reading: Each foreground cell gets a 2 placed diagonally up-left of it (wrapping around the grid edges, not over foreground); the result is then tiled 3x3.

new_rows.name: ul_wrap
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
upy(Y, Y2) :- px(Y, X, C), Y > 0, Y2 = Y - 1.
upy(Y, Y2) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0, my(Y2).
leftx(X, X2) :- px(Y, X, C), X > 0, X2 = X - 1.
leftx(X, X2) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0, mx(X2).
ul_wrap(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), upy(Y, Y2), leftx(X, X2), !fgc(Y2, X2).

why: output is 3x3 copies of the input with 2 at the (toroidally) up-left neighbour of every fg cell

reading: The single cell whose colour occurs exactly once is kept, everything else is cleared, and a 3x3 ring of 2 is drawn around that cell.

new_rows.name: uniq
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
uniq(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), N = 1.

why: exactly one colour appears once; output = that cell with its 8 neighbours set to 2, all else 0
invariants: position and colour of the unique cell

reading: Square blocks of background (3x3 first, then 2x2 ones not overlapping a 3x3) are filled with 1.

new_rows.name: zero_square
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).
sq2(Y, X) :- z(Y, X), Y1 = Y + 1, X1 = X + 1, z(Y, X1), z(Y1, X), z(Y1, X1).
sq3(Y, X) :- sq2(Y, X), Y1 = Y + 1, X1 = X + 1, sq2(Y, X1), sq2(Y1, X), sq2(Y1, X1).
in3(Y2, X2) :- sq3(Y, X), z(Y2, X2), Y3 = Y + 2, X3 = X + 2, Y2 >= Y, Y2 <= Y3, X2 >= X, X2 <= X3.
bad2(Y, X) :- sq2(Y, X), Y1 = Y + 1, X1 = X + 1, in3(Y2, X2), Y2 >= Y, Y2 <= Y1, X2 >= X, X2 <= X1.
good2(Y, X) :- sq2(Y, X), !bad2(Y, X).
zero_square(Y, X) :- in3(Y, X).
zero_square(Y2, X2) :- good2(Y, X), z(Y2, X2), Y1 = Y + 1, X1 = X + 1, Y2 >= Y, Y2 <= Y1, X2 >= X, X2 <= X1.

why: filled cells are exactly the greedy largest-first non-overlapping all-background squares of side >= 2 (matches 3x3 then non-overlapping 2x2 on all pairs)
invariants: background cells not in such a square

reading: Each colour-1 object is classified: closed (hole fully enclosed, or solid) objects slide to the left border and turn 2; objects with a hole open to the outside slide to the right border and turn 3. Rows are kept.

slots.subject: each colour-1 object
slots.test: does its internal background hole leak to the outside (gap in the outline)?
slots.closed or solid: move horizontally to the left border, recolour 2
slots.open: move horizontally to the right border, recolour 3

why: each object keeps its shape and rows; side and colour depend only on whether its hole is enclosed

reading: Inside the bounding box of the colour-8 cells, every 1 becomes 3; nothing else changes.

new_rows.name: box8
new_rows.datalog:
e(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 8.
y0(min(Y)) :- e(Y, X).
y1(max(Y)) :- e(Y, X).
x0(min(X)) :- e(Y, X).
x1(max(X)) :- e(Y, X).
box8(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), y0(A), y1(B), x0(D), x1(E), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= D, X <= E.

why: key is 1->3 (8 and 0 fixed); only cells within the 8 bounding box change (note 1 is the most common colour in pair 3, so the row uses px)
